Thanks again for the demo earlier — great signal on how the triage workflow will be used. Ahead of our MAP checkpoint next week I pulled together a short template to reconcile the token/unit economics assumptions so procurement and engineering have the same baseline.

Quick asks so we can finalize the MAP by Friday:

- B: average tokens per request by request type (intent classification, full-note generation, summary).

I attached a lightweight template (redwood_token-econ-template.xlsx) with the cells we typically use to produce a tokens/$ playbook. If you prefer, we can plug in the numbers and return a clean MAP sheet for signatures.

What I'll produce once we have inputs:
- reconciliation tab mapping your sample traffic -> tokens/day -> cost/day with current hosted pricing and a Dedicated tier estimate,
- sensitivity scenarios for 3 batching/prefetch configurations,
- a short one-page decision memo for procurement explaining tradeoffs and recommended guardrails for the pilot.

If you can drop the sample traffic and a couple example payloads by EOD Wednesday I can get the simulations back before our MAP review.

Thanks,

Thanks — received the sample traffic and the payloads. I ran a first-pass sim and attached the updated MAP (SageHealth_MAP_v3.xlsx) plus the simulation CSV (token-econ-sim-outputs.csv). Highlights:

- Baseline (no caching, minimal batching): ~ $3.8k/day hosted estimate at expected weekday load.
- With prefix caching on summaries and a modest batching window (20ms), cost reduces ~ 28% for identical quality.
- Prefetching warm cache for returning sessions (we model conservative hit rate 18%) lowers peak GPU concurrency and keeps 95th latency in the 220–300ms band for web flows.

Open assumptions I flagged in the MAP:
1) Request mix sensitivity — if full-note generation % > 8% of requests, unit cost rises sharply; we included a pivot table.
2) Batching latency trade — aggressive batch windows (>=50ms) further reduce cost but increase 95th tail; I added an ops guardrail recommendation.
3) Cost buckets — I show hosted vs Dedicated reserved monthly commit options; for your projected run-rate the Dedicated tier breaks even in ~9 months under our mid-case.

Next steps:
- Rishi, can you confirm the Dedicated latency SLO we can commit to for pilot if they go reserved?
- Priyom, I'll need a short paragraph for procurement explaining how our fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant would affect quality during capacity events.

Emily / Tom, if the numbers here look sensible, I'd propose we update the MAP in the Drive link and run one quick A/B sim with your weekend traffic slice (lower QPS, higher batch benefit) before the MAP signoff.

Cheers,
Karthik

Attachments: SageHealth_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub, 96KB); token-econ-sim-outputs.csv (CSV stub, 42KB)
